views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the line and signal willingness to return to the negotiating table without making new concessions. Do not escalate further in response to the US List 4 hike to 15% (effective Sept 1) — further retaliation would deepen self-inflicted damage on our more trade-exposed economy and feed Washington's decoupling narrative. Instead, maintain our measured $75B response and let the mounting pressure building inside the US economy (inverted curve, Fed cuts, crumbling consumer sentiment) bring the Americans back to the table on more favorable terms.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high but not existential. US tariffs at 25% on ~$250B and 15% on the remaining ~$300B are biting the real economy: our industrial production growth slid from 106.3 to 104.4 y/y (June-Aug), PPI went negative for the first time in three years, the manufacturing PMI sits at 49.7 (contraction), and Q2 GDP at 6.2% is the weakest in 27 years (web/country_health). Exports to the US fell 6.5% in July and the RMB broke 7 per dollar after Hanoi's currency-manipulator designation, while Huawei remains on the Entity List with Google and chip suppliers cut off. Offsetting the existential anchor are strong buffers — reserves are steady near $3.1T and the discount rate is unchanged at 2.9%, so financial stability holds. This justifies a ~+0.55 threat score. On action: further escalation would hurt us more than the US (we are more export-dependent), and the US side is already signalling distress — the 10Y yield collapsed to 1.47% with an inverted curve, the Fed cut rates, and consumer sentiment plunged from ~98 to 89.8. That US pressure is our leverage; patience and a firm-but-open negotiating posture (action_score +0.1, negotiate) is the disciplined play rather than either escalating or capitulating.
